name: Subset Sum with small doubling via constructive Freiman (Randolph-Wegrzycki)
description: Randolph and Wegrzycki parameterize integer sets by the doubling constant C = |A+A|/|A|. They make Freiman's theorem efficiently constructive (a covering GAP in near-linear FPT time), and use it to solve Binary ILP, hence Subset Sum, in n^{O_C(1)}, Unbounded Subset Sum in n^{O_C(log log log n)}, and k-SUM in near-linear time. An FPT (poly(n) times f(C)) Subset Sum algorithm is shown equivalent to a major open problem in ILP.
authors_year_venue: Tim Randolph, Karol Wegrzycki; 2024; arXiv:2407.18228 (title: Parameterized Algorithms on Integer Sets with Small Doubling: Integer Programming, Subset Sum and k-SUM). Venue: not stated in the version read [uncertain].
status_and_verification: Preprint v1 read via alphaXiv: abstract, Sec 1 (all contributions), Sec 3 (Thm 3.1, 3.2), Sec 5 (C-Subset Sum, Lemma 5.1, Thm 1.2), Sec 6 (Lemma 6.1, Thm 6.1), Sec 7 end, Appendix A start (Plunnecke-Ruzsa, Ruzsa modeling). Proofs of Thm 3.2 itself (Appendix A) and Sec 4 were only skimmed.
key_theorem_or_bound: Thm 3.2: for A of n integers with |A+A| <= C|A|, there is an O~_C(n) randomized algorithm (success 1-n^{-gamma}) returning a GAP P containing A of dimension d(C) and volume v(C)|A|, with d(C)=2^{C^{O(1)}}, v(C)=2^{2^{C^{O(1)}}}. Thm 1.1: C-Binary ILP in n^{O_C(1)} poly(|I|). Cor 5.1: C-Subset Sum in n^{O_C(1)}. Thm 1.2: C-Subset Sum in O_C(poly(n)) iff Hyperplane-Constrained Binary ILP in Delta^{O(m)} O_m(poly|I|). Thm 6.1: Unbounded C-Subset Sum in n^{O_C(log log log n)}. Cor 7.1: (C,4)-SUM in O~(Cn).
regime_exponents: Polynomial n^{O_C(1)}, where the exponent depends on C through f(C) with a tower-type dependence (d(C) doubly exponential via 2^{C^{O(1)}}, volume 2^{2^{C^{O(1)}}}). Since C <= n/2 + o(1) always, a bound with C = Theta(n) is vacuous; paper notes ETH forbids 2^{o(C)} n^{o(C/log C)}. No relation to 0.311n, 0.5n, 0.661n; conversely the paper's lower bound says C-Subset Sum cannot beat 2^{o(C)}.
proof_type_and_tools: Algebraic/geometry-of-numbers additive combinatorics: Ruzsa's proof of Freiman's theorem (Zhao's exposition) made algorithmic: Ruzsa modeling lemma (map to Z_q), Plunnecke-Ruzsa inequality |sX - tX| <= C^{s+t}|X|, Bogolyubov-Ruzsa, lattice/geometry of numbers. Subset Sum step: Freiman map to d(C) coordinates, then DP / Binary ILP with bounded coefficients and the hyperplane constraint <Ax,s>=t; Eisenbrand-Weismantel small-support lemma for the unbounded case.
quantitative_loss: Severe in C: GAP dimension and volume are double/triple exponential in C^{O(1)} (authors do not optimize; suspect Sanders/Schoen-type bounds improve it). Subset-Sum exponent n^{O_C(1)} is polynomial for constant C but at polynomial doubling C = n^{c} the function f(C) is astronomically large, so the bound does not survive even C = log n.
worst_case_vs_average_case: Worst case over all integer sets with doubling <= C (randomized for the construction, Monte Carlo with 1-n^{-gamma} success). No random-input assumption; but the hypothesis rules out generic (Sidon-like) inputs where C ~ n/2.
coefficient_set: {0,1} subset sums (binary ILP), also unbounded multiplicities, and variants with polynomially bounded variables.
subset_size_regime: All subsets for Subset Sum; separate fixed-k result for k-SUM with running time O~(C^{ceil(k/2)} 2^{O(k)} n). No Theta(n)-subsets analysis.
relevance_to_Nc: Indirect. Constant doubling implies few distinct subset sums (Freiman: at most n^{f(C)} sums) and hence huge bins (N_c very large; large-bin branch of C1 holds trivially). So it supplies the structured end of the dichotomy: if the whole input has small doubling, C1's large-bin regime applies and there is an efficient algorithm. It says nothing about N_c for polynomial doubling.
relevance_to_Dstar: Constant doubling forces |Sigma(2^X)| <= n^{f(C)}, so D* is at most polynomial: this is the extreme D* << 2^{0.311n} case of C2, and it is solved in n^{O_C(1)}. The constructive Freiman theorem is the branch 'few balanced half-sums -> efficient algorithm' only in the polynomially-many-sums extreme; it does not cover D* between n^{O(1)} and 2^{0.311n} [uncertain].
applicability_gap: (1) Needs C = O(1); the repo regime has polynomial doubling (C = n^c), where d(C), v(C) blow up and Freiman gives no useful GAP. (2) The doubling constant is of the whole input set A, while D* concerns sums of Theta(n)-subsets (sets of subset sums), a different object (iterated sumset of {0,w_i}). (3) The set of subset sums of A+... has doubling that scales as (n choose k) type, never constant for generic inputs. (4) FPT in C is shown equivalent to an open ILP problem, so even constant-C improvement beyond XP is blocked.
counterexample_or_hard_instance_family: Sidon-like sets have C about n/2 (the maximum), so the technique gives nothing; the paper cites that k-SUM hardness lives on Sidon-like sets (Abboud-Bringmann-Fischer, Jin-Xu). Hard instances for C-Subset Sum: any instance with C = Omega(log n / log log n) is not covered by the n^{O_C(1)} claim as a polynomial bound. AP-free is not discussed.
dependency_chain: Plunnecke-Ruzsa -> Ruzsa modeling -> constructive Freiman (this paper) -> binary ILP with bounded coefficients; links to BSG-type structure (constructive BSG of Chan-Lewenstein) when only energy is large, as in 'bsg_energy_and_pfr'; for Z-valued sets, Freiman precedes the algorithmic PFR (F_2^n) analogue.
constructiveness: Yes: O~_C(n) randomized with failure probability n^{-gamma}, but the hidden f(C) is 2^{2^{C^{O(1)}}}-type; subset-sum solving then costs n^{O_C(1)}. Verification of the GAP is trivial.
lean_formalizable: Low-to-moderate: Plunnecke-Ruzsa and Ruzsa covering lemma are formalizable without mathlib at the finite-set level, but Freiman's theorem (geometry of numbers/Minkowski) is heavy; the constructive near-linear time analysis is not formalizable cheaply.
computational_check: Source has no experiments. In-repo check at n<=40 is trivially possible for doubling of the input set and |Sigma(2^A)|, but the theorem is asymptotic in C; repo scripts could at best measure doubling constant C of hard instances and verify it is polynomial in n.
next_experiment: For the repo's candidate hard instances (random density-1, rank-d GAP with random generators), compute C = |A+A|/|A| and the doubling of the subset-sum set 2^A sums at n <= 30 to confirm doubling is polynomial and outside the n^{O_C(1)} window; then test whether C=n^{c} GAP instances have D* small.
open_issues: FPT in C is open and equivalent to a ILP breakthrough; dependence d(C), v(C) unoptimized; a (C,k)-SUM C^{ceil(k/2)} gap remains (Petridis improvement partly addresses). No known extension to C growing with n.
